correctness.rationale: Each output coordinate is a meet-preserving scalar chain map; its upward upper-level sets F_0,F_1 are nested principal filters (or empty). Pos evaluated at z=zero vector is equivalent to F_0 present with generator a in {-1,0}^n. Con requires that x∨t≥b implies x≥b for all t in {-1,0}^n; it fails iff some upper threshold coordinate b_j=0 and holds for b in {-1,1}^n. Thus disjoint Type I choices 2^n and Type II choices 3^n per component, and normality chooses only Type II. n=1,2 exhaustively compared to every scalar truth table (3^3 and 3^9 functions), checking actual MK/Pos/Con and threshold forms. General n relies on complete filter proof, not finite extrapolation. For n=1, M=5,N=3; n=2 M=169,N=81.
